ai.headline: OpenAI & Broadcom unveil Jalapeño: first custom inference ASIC, designed in 9 months with AI assistance
ai.body: Jalapeño is an inference-only ASIC co-designed by OpenAI and Broadcom in nine months using AI-assisted development, targeting gigawatt-scale deployments with 'substantially better than state-of-the-art' performance per watt. OpenAI aims to power 10 GW of compute with custom silicon by 2029, reducing Nvidia dependency for serving workloads while keeping Nvidia for training. This is a direct vertical integration play: owning silicon, models, and products lets each layer be tuned for the others.

ai.headline: Gemini 3.5 Flash gets native computer-use capabilities for agentic desktop automation
ai.body: Google launched computer-use natively in Gemini 3.5 Flash, enabling the lightweight model to drive desktop interfaces via continuous screenshot processing and action execution (click, scroll, type). Shipping in a cost-efficient Flash model rather than a frontier model signals Google is commoditising agentic UI automation. Directly competes with Anthropic's computer-use and emerging browser-agent frameworks.

ai.headline: Anthropic's Mythos model found vulnerabilities in classified US government systems under Project Glasswing
ai.body: A US official confirmed Anthropic's Mythos model, tested with intelligence agencies, rapidly identified vulnerabilities in classified systems but was not demonstrated exploiting them. The Trump administration responded with export controls and access restrictions on Anthropic's latest models, prompting the company to take models offline. Security leaders argue these restrictions weaken US cyber defences against adversaries who face no equivalent limitations.

ai.headline: Mechanistic explanation of prompt injection: models assess authority by text style, not role tags
ai.body: A LessWrong post provides a mechanistic account of why LLMs remain vulnerable to prompt injection: models learn to assess authority from writing style and content rather than from structural role tags (user/assistant/think), making it trivial to hijack control flow via injected text. This has direct implications for any agentic system that processes untrusted content — the problem is architectural, not patchable with prompt guards alone. Understanding this is prerequisite to designing secure agentic pipelines.

ai.headline: NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel delivers 3.7x fine-tuning throughput gains for MoE models via Expert Parallelism
ai.body: NVIDIA launched NeMo AutoModel on Hugging Face targeting MoE fine-tuning (Qwen3, DeepSeek V3), using Expert Parallelism and DeepEP fused communication kernels to distribute expert weights across GPU clusters. Benchmarks show 3.7x training throughput increase and 32% peak GPU memory reduction vs. native Transformers v5. Relevant for any team running large-scale fine-tuning who holds NVDA.

sec.headline: FortiBleed: Russian IAB brute-forced 430k FortiGate firewalls, harvested 110M credentials across 24 protocols
sec.body: Active since February, FortiBleed deployed FortigateSniffer to capture credentials across 24 protocols, feeding a Golang-based CyberStrike Harvester pipeline that cracks hashes via Hashcat/Hashtopolis, ranks targets by economic value, and resells access. The operation replants harvested credentials across thousands of devices to maintain persistence. Any organisation running FortiGate appliances should audit for anomalous authentication patterns and rotate credentials immediately.

sec.headline: DifyTap: four CVEs (CVSS 9.1 & 9.4) in Dify LLMOps platform expose cross-tenant data and arbitrary API access
sec.body: Zafran Security disclosed four vulnerabilities in Dify (used by 1M+ apps): CVE-2026-41947 (CVSS 9.1) lacks tenant validation in tracing config; CVE-2026-41948 (CVSS 9.4) enables arbitrary API access and path traversal via the plugin daemon; two high-severity CVEs affect file identification and permissions. Any signed-up console user could read other tenants' chats, files, and internal APIs in multi-tenant cloud deployments. Fixed in Dify 1.14.2; WAF rule recommended for CVE-2026-41948.

sec.headline: Woodgnat/KongTuke IAB links ModeloRAT and disk-less Backdoor.Mistic to Qilin, Akira, Black Basta ransomware chains
sec.body: Symantec and Zscaler attribute Python-based ModeloRAT (RC4 C2 via signed pythonw.exe) and new in-memory Backdoor.Mistic (DLL-sideloaded as EndpointDlp.dll via MpExtMs.exe, with self-delete kill switch) to financially motivated broker Woodgnat. ClickFix/Microsoft Teams helpdesk lures seed multiple ransomware families. Hunt for EndpointDlp.dll loads by MpExtMs.exe and remote-tool-named Run-key persistence.

sec.headline: Cordyceps: 300+ exploitable GitHub Actions chains found in repos from Microsoft, Google, Apache, Cloudflare, PSF
sec.body: Novee scanned ~30,000 prominent OSS repos and confirmed over 300 exploitable CI/CD chains where attackers with a free GitHub account can trigger workflows via PRs or comments to steal long-lived tokens and push malicious artifacts into production paths including Azure Sentinel, Google Cloud, Apache Doris, and Black's Docker images. The blast radius reaches thousands of downstream environments. Immediate audit of workflow triggers and token scopes is warranted.

sec.headline: Cloudflare open-sources security-audit-skill: multi-agent vulnerability discovery pipeline with adversarial review
sec.body: Cloudflare's security-audit-skill transforms a coding agent into a six-phase security auditor (recon, hunt, validate, report, JSON output, independent verification) where the validating agent is never the finder, reducing false positives. A single run detects ~50% of vulnerabilities; repeated passes are required for comprehensive coverage. Open-source and composable with existing findings to skip known issues.

fin.headline: Mastercard and PrivatBank complete Ukraine's first AI-agent-executed payment using governed agentic framework
fin.body: Mastercard's agentic framework brings AI agents into the payment flow as authenticated, visible participants with each transaction secured, transparent, and auditable. This is the first production deployment of a governed agentic payment in Ukraine, positioning Mastercard as the identity and trust layer for agentic commerce. Direct signal for how payment identity and authorisation will need to evolve as agents become payment principals.

fin.headline: Stripe Directory public preview: machine-readable network for agents to discover, provision, and pay for services
fin.body: Stripe Directory is a searchable directory enabling developers and AI agents to discover businesses, services, and machine payment endpoints, then programmatically provision integrations and pay via Stripe's machine payment rails. This positions Stripe as the service-discovery and payment infrastructure layer for agentic commerce — analogous to DNS but for agent-to-agent transactions. Significant for anyone building multi-agent systems that need to transact autonomously.

fin.headline: Modern Treasury + Sardine partnership adds pre-transaction fraud signals to payment orchestration
fin.body: Modern Treasury integrated Sardine's device intelligence, behavioural biometrics, and transaction monitoring into its payment operations platform, enabling fraud detection earlier in the payment lifecycle rather than post-settlement. Relevant for fintech teams evaluating layered fraud stacks on top of payment orchestration layers.

fin.headline: ICE and OKX form 50-50 JV to tokenise NYSE equities and ICE futures on regulated broker-dealer infrastructure
fin.body: Intercontinental Exchange (NYSE parent) and OKX are building a regulated US broker-dealer and futures commission merchant for on-chain tokenised NYSE equities and ICE futures, pending regulatory approval. This pairs ICE's regulated exchange footprint with OKX's global crypto customer base, accelerating TradFi's migration to on-chain market infrastructure. Portfolio-relevant: AMZN (AWS cloud likely infrastructure) and broader market structure shift.

fin.headline: Micron posts record Q3 revenue of $41.5B (vs $9.3B prior year) on data centre memory and storage demand
fin.body: Micron's Q3 revenue of $41.5B — a 4.5x year-over-year increase — driven entirely by data centre memory and storage demand, with better-than-expected Q4 guidance. Shortages are causing price increases affecting electronics manufacturers. Strong leading indicator for continued AI infrastructure build-out; relevant for NVDA and TSMC holdings.

swe.headline: ByteByteGo deep-dive: service architecture anti-patterns trace to one early decomposition decision
swe.body: The post argues that nearly all microservice anti-patterns (latency, partial failure, distributed data consistency issues) trace back to premature service splitting rather than a catalog of independent mistakes. The framing — that a service must control its own data and that network calls fundamentally change failure semantics — is a useful forcing function for staff-level design reviews. Practical guidance on recognising when individually reasonable decomposition decisions accumulate into an unworkable architecture.

swe.headline: Johnson & Johnson MSAL client-side bypass and hardcoded AWS key exposed ~1,000 student records; ATMS fix delayed 6 months
swe.body: A researcher bypassed J&J's campus recruiting site by circumventing client-side MSAL checks and using a hardcoded AWS API key. The ATMS app exposed user lists and admin access via unauthenticated APIs and local-storage spoofing. Disclosure timeline shows the ATMS was only fixed after journalist contact, with delays from October 2025 to April 2026 — a useful case study in client-side auth anti-patterns and disclosure dynamics.

mkt.headline: Google suffering sustained senior AI talent exodus to Anthropic and rivals
mkt.body: Gemini researchers Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel joined Anthropic, following Noam Shazeer and DeepMind director John Jumper in a wave of high-profile departures from Google's AI divisions. Sustained talent bleed at this seniority level is a structural risk to GOOGL's AI roadmap, particularly for Gemini's research velocity. Relevant for assessing the durability of Google's AI competitive position.

mkt.headline: Amazon v. Perplexity lawsuit over Comet browser agent identity spoofing raises foundational agentic web precedent
mkt.body: Amazon is suing Perplexity, alleging Comet browser identifies itself as Chrome rather than an agent, violating Amazon Store conditions of use. The case tests whether sites can contractually mandate agent identification — a question with wide implications for agentic commerce, bot management, and IAM for non-human identities on the open web. The outcome could shape how agent identity is governed across all major platforms.

mkt.headline: Visa and Mastercard fend off state and federal fee restrictions; interchange fight continues
mkt.body: Colorado and Illinois state-level interchange fee restrictions stalled and a federal court approved a contested merchant settlement, preserving Visa and Mastercard's network fee structures. Despite sustained retailer and legislative pressure, the card networks and issuing banks have maintained their grip. Removes a near-term regulatory headwind for network fee revenue.

deepDives.title: Cordyceps: 300+ Exploitable GitHub Actions Chains in Microsoft, Google, Apache, Cloudflare Repos
deepDives.why: Primary security research with a specific exploitable finding list — immediately actionable for any team using GitHub Actions CI/CD, covering token theft and supply chain artifact poisoning at scale.

deepDives.title: A Mechanistic Explanation of Prompt Injection (and Why You Should Study Roles)
deepDives.why: First-principles mechanistic account of why role tags fail to enforce authority boundaries in LLMs — essential reading for anyone designing security controls in agentic or LLM-integrated systems.

deepDives.title: Stripe Directory Public Preview — Machine Payment Rails for Agentic Commerce
deepDives.why: Official Stripe documentation for a new primitive that enables agent-to-agent service discovery and payment — directly relevant to anyone building or securing agentic fintech infrastructure.
